Satellite imagery, GIS, GPS, and drones all provide the ability to gather information about the scene. However, when a disaster happens indoors, none of those capabilities carry over. The available data becomes 2D, typically a blueprint if it exists, and does not include standpipes, shutoffs, alarm panels, or AEDs. These missing elements are necessary for a safe and timely response by first responders. Without indoor spatial intelligence, responders must make high stakes and high-risk decisions with incomplete information. Fixing the issue requires data that cannot be produced at scale and currently relies on manual documentation. However, many of these structures do not meet current building code requirements and require strategic upgrades. To address this vulnerability, NIST is actively developing best practices, design recommendations, and guidelines for utilizing building retrofit systems to improve the performance of existing structures. Beyond individual structures, it is critical to understand how different retrofit schemes and targets impact the community recovery. NIST is leading ongoing projects to quantify and measure the impact of various retrofit strategies at the community level. By developing the fundamental measurement science needed to assess retrofitted building performance, this work directly supports the long-term resilience and rapid recovery of communities following natural hazards. pages.text: Bunion facts: Causes, symptoms, and treatment | National Geographic Premium HEALTH Why do we have bunions? Blame an evolutionary toe failure. For millennia, people have suffered from bunions, a painful condition that’s uniquely human. Here’s why—and how to ease the pain. A colored x-ray image highlights bunions in the feet of a 54-year-old patient. The foot deformity may affect up to a quarter of the modern adult population. ZEPHYR/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY By Erin Blakemore Last updated October 14, 2025 Bunions have plagued human feet since ancient times. A brief glimpse at archaeology and history points to their presence, from prehistoric footprints in England to ancient Egyptian mummies with bony bumps . A whopping 27 percent of burials in and around Cambridge, England, during the 14th and 15th centuries showed skeletal evidence of bunions, compared with just 6 percent in earlier centuries. Year-over-year employment and payroll changes are calculated between the same point in year t and year t-1 (i.e., June 12 th year t-1 to June 12 th year t, etc.). Employment and payroll growth is labeled as job and pay creation respectively and employment and payroll decline as job and pay destruction. A novel innovation in the BDS-SU-REV is the incorporation of annual revenue data for single-establishment firms that consistently maintain positive employment levels each quarter. pages.text: Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data Skip Navigation Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data July 13, 2026 The Business Trends and Outlook Survey provides high-frequency, nationally representative data on U.S. employer businesses. The survey provides local, state, and federal officials near real-time data for policy and decision-making including after natural disasters or during economic crises. The BTOS also provides insights into business recovery after these events. The BTOS sample consists of approximately 1.2 million businesses split into six panels (approximately 200,000 cases per panel). pages.description: Peter Bradshaw: Reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes.
pages.text: But I'm a Cheerleader | Movies | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Movies This article is more than 25 years old Review But I'm a Cheerleader This article is more than 25 years old Peter Bradshaw Thu 12 Apr 2001 21.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google D irector and co-writer Jamie Babbit makes her feature debut with this satire of America's creepy Christian "sexual reorientation" camps, where confused teens are sent so that their nascent gayness can be deprogrammed out of them. Natasha Lyonne plays Megan, a cheerleader who hugs her fellow pom-pom-botherers inappropriately and hates making out with her jock boyfriend. He and Megan's family arrange an "intervention" where she is confronted with her shameful tendencies and sent to the True Directions camp, run by two smug tyrants in Straight Is Great T-shirts, played by Cathy Moriarty and RuPaul (here out of drag), clearly repressed gays themselves. Once there, Megan falls for a girl with the interesting name of Graham, played by Clea DuVall. As in all therapy boot-camp movies - such as Girl, Interrupted, in which DuVall had a role - there has to be a wild child with whom the heroine makes a connection. This is Graham's role. It's reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes. But it could have been funnier, and I would have preferred to know more in documentary terms about the actual reality of these terrible camps, rather than sit through this heavy-handed and oddly lenient comedy. pages.title: By Land and Sea—17 European Trips From London | National Geographic
pages.description: Whether it’s a short hop across the Channel or an overland expedition to the furthest reaches of Europe, some of the richest travel experiences happen when you skip the flight.
pages.text: By Land and Sea—17 European Trips From London | National Geographic By Oliver Smith Published October 24, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Today, it’s easier to travel further and faster around Europe than ever before — to board a flight and effectively parachute yourself into a new destination. But by travelling overland, be it by ferry, train or car, on a bike or on foot, you’re able to observe the slow, subtle changes at ground level with every accumulated mile. Overland travel by rail is also easier than it’s ever been, thanks to an ever-expanding network of high-speed and sleeper trains across Europe. You might board a morning Eurostar at London St Pancras International and that same day be joining a midnight crawl of Madrid’s tapas bars or standing beneath Milan’s hulking Duomo as stars twinkle above its white marble facade. Ferries, too, offer perspectives unfamiliar to those at the cruising altitude of an airliner, whether that’s witnessing the green coast of northern Spain unravelling out of the blue horizons of Biscay or seeing Icelandic volcanoes peek over grey North Atlantic waves. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/calibration-services Standards Calibration services Sign Up to Get NIST News GovDelivery Purchase calibrations Learn more about calibrations NIST on a Chip If you need to measure something, NIST is the go-to place for help. And NIST is also the place to go if you need to calibrate your measuring equipment. In our everyday lives, calibrations are often the little adjustments you may make, for example to make sure the colors of your computer monitor or television are accurate, so it will show photos or videos the way that a filmmaker or photographer intended. But for a scientific measurement laboratory such as NIST, calibrations are a bit different. NIST calibrations determine a relationship between the measurement standard (like the Kibble balance) and that instrument or object (such as a cylindrical metal kilogram mass). By using a world-class reference such as the Kibble balance, calibrations make it possible for a piece of measuring equipment to make the most accurate measurement it can. From MRIs to lasers, NIST's calibration services are part of many aspects of everyday life. While many are familiar with the Oregon Trail, the California Trail is equally legendary, filled with stories of hope, hardships, and transformation. This historic route stretched thousands of miles across the West, turning travelers’ dreams and Native American ways of life into destinies marked by both gain and loss. Between 1841 and 1869, thousands of pioneers traveled nearly 2,000 miles from the Missouri River to the Sierra Nevada Mountains and beyond. Driven by hopes of fertile land, religious freedom, and gold, their journey was far from easy. Along the way, they faced disease, conflict, and dangerous terrain, including the infamous Donner Party disaster. Despite these hardships, people kept coming, lured by the promise of prosperity and adventure. Visit the California Trail Interpretive Center in Elko, Nevada, to explore the people and stories behind this epic journey. Dingell Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act (Public Law 116-9 also known as the Dingell Act), a comprehensive public land management bill with over 170 separate sections that affect almost every state in the nation. The Act has a number of California-specific provisions, including the Santa Ana River Wash Plan Land Exchange and California Desert Protection and Recreation. The Santa Ana River Wash Plan Land Exchange section directs the Department of the Interior to exchange BLM-managed public land in San Bernardino County for lands owned by the San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District. The exchange would consolidate land ownership to facilitate mineral development, flood control, groundwater recharge, recreation, and improved habitat for threatened and endangered species. Please be considerate of the next visitor, and confine all motorized and mountain bike travel to designated roads and trails. The Scot, 37, needed an operation for an injury sustained repeatedly punching a drinks table on stage following his first-round exit at the PDC World Championships last December. And he made headlines during the summer after requiring medical attention during his World Matchplay encounter with Ross Smith, which he had to forfeit. His dizzy turn was put down to high blood pressure caused by dehydration. "I didn't know what it was, I looked at the board and I just felt like everything was spinning," Menzies told BBC Scotland. "They took me off the stage, there were paramedics and first aid on site and they were taking my blood pressure and it was up to over 200, and they were going to phone an ambulance because that was like heart attack material. "But as soon as they gave me a drink of water it dropped massively. Illustration by Roche How do scientists know which insects can see color? John Jay Rouse | St. Cloud, Minnesota Much of what we know about which colors insects can see is based on a combination of behavioral studies and understanding the morphology and physiology of the insect eye. The compound eye found in most insects is made up of a few to thousands of individual units called ommatidia, and each ommatidium includes a rhabdom, a transparent structure under the lens, which stores photosensitive pigments known as opsins that are used for detecting colors. The more kinds and combinations of opsins an insect’s rhabdom has, the more colors it can see. Most insects can only see a narrow spectrum of colors, if any at all.
